project.name: mesmo
project.description: MESMO (Multi-Energy System Modeling and Optimization) is an open-source Python tool for modeling, simulation, and optimization of multi-scale electric and thermal distribution systems together with distributed energy resources (DERs). Note: this project has over 100 source files; consider scoping analysis to a subdirectory for faster results.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Package barrel for the MESMO library; re-exports the primary sub-modules (api, config, data_interface, der_models, grid models, problems, solutions, utils, plots) so users can `import mesmo`.

nodes.name: api.py
nodes.summary: High-level convenience API exposing one-line entry points (`run_nominal_operation_problem`, `run_optimal_operation_problem`) that wire up data, solve a problem, and write results.

nodes.name: config_default.yml
nodes.summary: Default YAML configuration shipped with MESMO; defines paths, database, logging, optimization, parallel and plots sections consumed by `config.get_config`.

nodes.name: config.py
nodes.summary: Configuration loader built on Dynaconf; merges the default YAML with user overrides and provides helpers to resolve paths, obtain a logger, and lazily build a Ray parallel pool.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Dynaconf layered settings with user config override.

nodes.name: data_interface.py
nodes.summary: Ingests CSV scenario/grid/DER/price data into a SQLite database and hydrates structured pandas dataframes for scenarios, electric grids, thermal grids, DERs and prices used by downstream models.

nodes.name: data_schema.sql
nodes.summary: SQLite schema defining all MESMO input tables: scenarios, electric/thermal grid topology, DERs, price/timeseries, line/transformer types and linearization parameters.

nodes.name: der_models.py
nodes.summary: Distributed energy resource (DER) model hierarchy — fixed/flexible loads, EV chargers, generators, storage, flexible buildings, cooling/heating plants, CHP — plus the `DERModelSet` that assembles state-space and optimization constraints.

nodes.name: electric_grid_models.py
nodes.summary: Electric distribution grid modeling: admittance/incidence matrix construction, fixed-point / Z-bus / OpenDSS power flow solvers, and global & local linear sensitivity models with an associated model-set for multi-timestep optimization.
nodes.languageNotes: Mixes dense and sparse matrix representations; uses scipy.sparse heavily.

nodes.name: plots.py
nodes.summary: Plotting utilities for electric/thermal grid graphs, line/transformer/node utilization heatmaps and histograms, and aggregate DER timeseries using Plotly, Matplotlib and NetworkX.

nodes.name: problems.py
nodes.summary: Problem orchestration layer that composes DER, electric, and thermal models into `NominalOperationProblem` and `OptimalOperationProblem` objects, handles solve invocation and results aggregation.

nodes.name: solutions.py
nodes.summary: Generic optimization problem wrapper around CVXPY/Gurobi: registers variables/parameters/constraints/objectives, solves, and retrieves primal/dual values with support for sparse matrix formulations.

nodes.name: thermal_grid_models.py
nodes.summary: Thermal (district heating/cooling) grid modeling: topology + hydraulic matrices, explicit and Newton-Raphson thermal power flow solvers, and linear sensitivity model-sets for optimization.

nodes.name: utils.py
nodes.summary: Cross-cutting helpers — base result classes, Ray-based parallel starmap wrappers, timing logger, index/phase utilities, inverse-with-zeros matrix helper, results-path management, and Plotly export helpers.

nodes.name: conf.py
nodes.summary: Sphinx configuration for building the MESMO documentation site, wiring extensions, theme, autodoc settings and the `setup` hook.

nodes.name: run_nominal_operation_problem
nodes.summary: One-shot entry point: loads scenario data, constructs a NominalOperationProblem, solves it and persists results to disk.

nodes.name: run_optimal_operation_problem
nodes.summary: One-shot entry point: loads scenario data, constructs an OptimalOperationProblem, solves the optimization and persists results.

nodes.name: get_config
nodes.summary: Loads the default MESMO YAML settings via Dynaconf and merges any user-provided `config.yml` overrides.

nodes.name: parse_path
nodes.summary: Resolves configuration path strings, expanding relative references against the package root.

nodes.name: get_logger
nodes.summary: Creates a named logger honoring the configured log level and formatter settings.

nodes.name: get_parallel_pool
nodes.summary: Lazily initialises a Ray-based parallel execution pool using the configured number of workers.

nodes.name: recreate_database
nodes.summary: Rebuilds the SQLite database from scratch by applying the schema and re-importing every CSV file found under the configured data directories.

nodes.name: import_csv_file
nodes.summary: Imports a single CSV file into the corresponding SQLite table, replacing existing rows.

nodes.name: connect_database
nodes.summary: Opens a SQLite connection to the MESMO database, rebuilding it first if the file is missing.

nodes.name: ScenarioData
nodes.summary: Loads and cross-joins a scenario's top-level metadata, timestep index, parameters and associated timeseries.

nodes.name: DERData
nodes.summary: Loads DER definitions, type parameters and timeseries (loads, EV chargers, flexible buildings, storage) for a scenario.

nodes.name: ElectricGridData
nodes.summary: Loads electric grid topology: nodes, lines, transformers, line/transformer types and DER assignments.

nodes.name: ThermalGridData
nodes.summary: Loads thermal grid topology, line/pipe types and DER assignments for district heating/cooling networks.

nodes.name: PriceData
nodes.summary: Loads and resamples electricity/thermal price timeseries aligned to the scenario horizon.

nodes.name: DERModel
nodes.summary: Abstract base class for all distributed energy resource models; defines the state/control/output interface, timeseries and mapping matrices.

nodes.name: ConstantPowerModel
nodes.summary: Minimal DER representation with constant active/reactive power injections derived from its timeseries.

nodes.name: FixedLoadModel
nodes.summary: Non-controllable load DER: applies a fixed consumption timeseries as electrical load.

nodes.name: FixedEVChargerModel
nodes.summary: Non-controllable EV charger DER applying a fixed charging profile.

nodes.name: FixedGeneratorModel
nodes.summary: Non-controllable generator DER with a fixed output profile.

nodes.name: FlexibleDERModel
nodes.summary: Base class for controllable DERs: adds optimization variables and state-space dynamics on top of DERModel.

nodes.name: FlexibleLoadModel
nodes.summary: Deferrable/flexible load DER with controllable consumption, comfort constraints and energy-balance state-space dynamics.

nodes.name: FlexibleEVChargerModel
nodes.summary: Flexible EV charger DER modeling state-of-charge dynamics, charge/discharge bounds and departure constraints.

nodes.name: FlexibleGeneratorModel
nodes.summary: Controllable generator DER with ramping, minimum up/down times and dispatch constraints.

nodes.name: StorageModel
nodes.summary: Battery / thermal storage DER with state-of-charge dynamics, charge/discharge efficiencies and energy capacity limits.

nodes.name: FlexibleBuildingModel
nodes.summary: Wraps a CoBMo building model as a flexible DER, exposing thermal state-space and comfort constraints.

nodes.name: CoolingPlantModel
nodes.summary: District cooling plant DER coupling electric input to cooling thermal output via chiller COP and plant limits.

nodes.name: HeatingPlantModel
nodes.summary: District heating plant DER coupling fuel/electric input to heating thermal output.

nodes.name: FlexibleCHP
nodes.summary: Combined heat and power DER jointly producing electric and thermal output with coupled conversion constraints.

nodes.name: DERModelSet
nodes.summary: Aggregates all DER models for a scenario; constructs unified state-space matrices and injects DER variables/constraints into optimization problems.

nodes.name: make_der_models
nodes.summary: Factory that instantiates DER model objects for every DER in a scenario.

nodes.name: make_der_model
nodes.summary: Dispatches to the appropriate DER model subclass based on the DER type identifier.

nodes.name: ElectricGridModel
nodes.summary: Core electric grid model: builds branch/node admittance, incidence and DER mapping matrices from topology data and exposes primitive power-flow quantities.

nodes.name: ElectricGridModelDefault
nodes.summary: Concrete MESMO-native electric grid model using pandas/scipy admittance construction.

nodes.name: ElectricGridModelOpenDSS
nodes.summary: OpenDSS-backed electric grid model that rebuilds the DSS circuit and extracts admittance/incidence matrices for downstream use.

nodes.name: PowerFlowSolutionFixedPoint
nodes.summary: Fixed-point iteration power-flow solver handling wye/delta loads, generators and slack bus in unbalanced networks.

nodes.name: PowerFlowSolutionZBus
nodes.summary: Z-bus iterative power-flow solver formulated around current injections and the impedance matrix.

nodes.name: PowerFlowSolutionOpenDSS
nodes.summary: Power-flow solver that delegates to OpenDSS and translates back node voltages and branch flows.

nodes.name: PowerFlowSolutionSet
nodes.summary: Convenience container running power-flow over every timestep in a scenario, optionally in parallel.

nodes.name: LinearElectricGridModelBase
nodes.summary: Shared base for linear sensitivity electric grid models: defines voltage/branch-flow/loss sensitivity matrices versus DER power injections.

nodes.name: LinearElectricGridModelGlobal
nodes.summary: Global linearization around a reference power-flow solution producing LinDistFlow-style sensitivity matrices.

nodes.name: LinearElectricGridModelLocal
nodes.summary: Local (per-node) linearization of the electric grid around a reference power-flow operating point.

nodes.name: LinearElectricGridModelSet
nodes.summary: Multi-timestep linear electric grid model manager that injects grid variables, constraints and DLMP dual extraction into optimization problems.

nodes.name: ElectricGridGraph
nodes.summary: NetworkX graph wrapper for an electric grid model providing coordinates and plotting-friendly metadata.

nodes.name: ThermalGridGraph
nodes.summary: NetworkX graph wrapper for a thermal grid model with layout data for plotting utilities.

nodes.name: create_video
nodes.summary: Stitches a sequence of plot frames into an animation/video file for time-varying grid state.

nodes.name: plot_total_active_power
nodes.summary: Plots total active power timeseries across DERs and grid exchange on a single chart.

nodes.name: plot_histogram_cumulative_branch_utilization
nodes.summary: Cumulative histogram of branch (line/transformer) utilization across timesteps for grid stress analysis.

nodes.name: plot_histogram_node_utilization
nodes.summary: Histogram of node voltage utilization against operational bounds.

nodes.name: plot_aggregate_timeseries_der_power
nodes.summary: Aggregate DER power timeseries plot decomposed by DER type / phase.

nodes.name: ProblemBase
nodes.summary: Thin abstract base defining the `solve` / `get_results` contract shared by nominal and optimal operation problems.

nodes.name: ProblemDict
nodes.summary: Ordered dict of problems that are solved and post-processed together, used for multi-case studies.

nodes.name: NominalOperationProblem
nodes.summary: Deterministic operational simulation problem: runs power-flow against a nominal DER dispatch and collects grid/DER results.

nodes.name: OptimalOperationProblem
nodes.summary: Multi-period optimization problem coupling DER, electric and thermal models; builds the CVXPY/Gurobi problem and extracts DLMPs and results.

nodes.name: OptimizationProblem
nodes.summary: Generic optimization problem builder supporting variables/parameters/constraints/objectives in sparse-matrix form; dispatches to CVXPY or Gurobi and extracts primal/dual solutions.

nodes.name: ThermalGridModel
nodes.summary: Thermal grid model: builds branch/node incidence matrices, hydraulic parameters and DER mappings for district heating/cooling networks.

nodes.name: ThermalPowerFlowSolutionBase
nodes.summary: Abstract base for thermal power-flow solvers defining the node/branch output interface.

nodes.name: ThermalPowerFlowSolutionExplicit
nodes.summary: Closed-form explicit thermal power-flow solver using linear hydraulic assumptions.

nodes.name: ThermalPowerFlowSolutionNewtonRaphson
nodes.summary: Newton-Raphson iterative thermal power-flow solver handling nonlinear friction head-loss.

nodes.name: ThermalPowerFlowSolution
nodes.summary: Factory dispatch selecting the configured thermal power-flow solver implementation.

nodes.name: ThermalPowerFlowSolutionSet
nodes.summary: Runs thermal power-flow over every timestep in a scenario, aggregating results.

nodes.name: LinearThermalGridModelBase
nodes.summary: Shared base defining thermal sensitivity matrices of node head/branch flow versus DER thermal power.

nodes.name: LinearThermalGridModelGlobal
nodes.summary: Global linearization of the thermal grid around a reference solution.

nodes.name: LinearThermalGridModelLocal
nodes.summary: Per-node local linearization of the thermal grid around a reference operating point.

nodes.name: LinearThermalGridModelSet

nodes.name: ObjectBase

tour.title: What Is MESMO?
tour.description: Start with the project README to understand MESMO's purpose: an open-source Python library for modeling, simulating, and optimizing multi-scale electric and thermal distribution systems with distributed energy resources (DERs). The README frames the four capability pillars the rest of the codebase implements — electric grid modeling, thermal grid modeling, DER modeling, and solution interfaces — and points to the documentation and example scripts we will walk through next.

tour.title: Package Entry & High-Level API
tour.description: The `mesmo` package exposes itself through `__init__.py`, a barrel module that re-exports every major subsystem (api, config, data_interface, der_models, electric_grid_models, thermal_grid_models, problems, solutions, utils, plots). `api.py` layers one-line convenience entry points on top — `run_nominal_operation_problem` and `run_optimal_operation_problem` — that assemble data, build a problem object, solve, and persist results. This pair is how most users interact with MESMO and sets up every other subsystem in this tour.
tour.languageLesson: Python package `__init__.py` files act as barrel modules: re-exporting submodules here lets users write `import mesmo` and access `mesmo.api`, `mesmo.der_models`, etc., without reaching into the filesystem layout.

tour.title: Configuration System
tour.description: MESMO is configuration-driven: paths, solver choices, logging levels, parallelization, and plot defaults all live in `config_default.yml`. `config.py` uses Dynaconf to merge that default YAML with user overrides and exposes helpers such as `get_config`, `get_logger`, and a lazy Ray parallel pool. Almost every other module in the library begins by fetching settings from here, which is why understanding configuration early makes later steps easier.
tour.languageLesson: YAML is whitespace-significant and maps naturally to nested Python dictionaries. Dynaconf layers multiple YAML files, environment variables, and programmatic overrides into a single settings object, which keeps library defaults intact while letting users customize without editing installed code.

tour.title: Data Interface & SQLite Schema
tour.description: Test cases enter MESMO as CSV files under `data/`. `data_interface.py` ingests those CSVs into a SQLite database defined by `data_schema.sql` and hydrates strongly-typed pandas dataframes for scenarios, grids, DERs, and price series. This is the boundary between raw user input and the numerical models that come next — every model constructor in later steps takes data produced by this module.
tour.languageLesson: SQL schemas are contracts: the table and column definitions in `data_schema.sql` dictate what the CSV loaders must produce and what the downstream Python models can assume. Using SQLite as an intermediate representation keeps scenario queries fast and makes the input format explicit.

tour.title: Electric Grid Modeling
tour.description: `electric_grid_models.py` is one of MESMO's two core physics modules. It builds admittance and incidence matrices for multi-phase unbalanced AC networks, runs non-linear power flow via fixed-point, Z-bus, or OpenDSS solvers, and derives global/local linear sensitivity models used later for convex optimization. The non-linear solvers give ground truth; the linearized model-sets make optimization tractable.

tour.title: Thermal Grid Modeling
tour.description: `thermal_grid_models.py` is the district heating/cooling counterpart to the electric grid module. It constructs topology and hydraulic matrices for radial thermal networks, solves thermal power flow explicitly and via Newton-Raphson, and exposes linear sensitivity model-sets with the same interface shape as the electric grid. That symmetry is what lets MESMO couple both commodities in a single multi-energy optimization later in the tour.

tour.title: Distributed Energy Resources
tour.description: `der_models.py` contains the largest single class hierarchy in the library: fixed and flexible loads, EV chargers, dispatchable generators, storage, flexible buildings, cooling/heating plants, and combined heat-and-power units. Each DER publishes both a time-series state-space representation and the optimization constraints needed to schedule it. `DERModelSet` aggregates these into the coupling layer that ties DERs to the electric and thermal grids from Steps 5 and 6.

tour.title: Problem & Solution Orchestration
tour.description: `problems.py` composes DER, electric, and thermal models into two high-level problem classes — `NominalOperationProblem` (simulation) and `OptimalOperationProblem` (optimization) — and aggregates results after solving. `solutions.py` is the generic CVXPY/Gurobi wrapper underneath, registering variables, parameters, constraints, and objectives, then retrieving primal and dual values. Together they turn the physics models into something a user can actually run.

tour.title: Visualization & Shared Utilities
tour.description: `plots.py` renders grid topology graphs, line/transformer/node utilization heatmaps, and DER timeseries using Plotly, Matplotlib, and NetworkX — the go-to module for turning results into figures. `utils.py` provides cross-cutting helpers used everywhere else in the library: base result classes, Ray-based parallel `starmap`, a `log_time` timing wrapper, index/phase helpers, a safe inverse-with-zeros routine, and results-path management. Its high fan-in (10 incoming edges) reflects how foundational it is.

tour.title: Using MESMO: End-to-End Examples
tour.description: Now that every subsystem is in view, these runnable scripts show them working together. `run_api_optimal_operation_problem.py` is the canonical one-call entry point. `run_multi_grid_optimal_operation.py` exercises the coupled electric–thermal optimization that justified the thermal/electric symmetry in Steps 5–6. `example_1.py` is the tutorial on-ramp, and `docs/examples.md` explains the narrative behind all three.

tour.title: Tests and Physics Validation
tour.description: MESMO distinguishes software tests from physics validation. `tests/test_api.py` and `tests/test_problems.py` are pytest modules that exercise the public API and each problem class end-to-end. Alongside them, the `examples/validation_*.py` scripts compare MESMO's linearized models and power flow solvers against reference tools like OpenDSS and against nonlinear ground truth — this is how the research-quality modeling claims in Steps 5–6 are defended.

tour.title: Packaging, CI & Deployment
tour.description: The final stop covers how MESMO is built, tested in CI, and distributed. `pyproject.toml` holds PEP 621 metadata and dependency declarations; `environment-ubuntu-latest.yml` pins the exact conda environment used by CI; `.github/workflows/pythontests.yml` runs the pytest suite across platforms; and the `Dockerfile` packages the whole toolchain into a reproducible container via `development_setup.py`. Together these make the scientific code reproducible on any machine — the non-negotiable requirement for research software.
tour.languageLesson: Reproducible scientific Python pairs `pyproject.toml` (what the package is) with a conda environment lockfile (exact versions of every transitive dependency, including native libraries like solvers). The Dockerfile encodes that same environment at the OS level, guaranteeing the CI pipeline and a user's laptop run identical code.
